menubar:analysis.label: Scale and offset Y…
menubar:analysis.title: Y′ = a·Y + b: a dark level to subtract, a gain to correct, a sign to flip.

menubar:analysis.label: Scale and offset X…
menubar:analysis.title: X′ = a·X + b. With a = −1, turns anti-Stokes shifts into Stokes shifts.

menubar:analysis.label: Normalize…
menubar:analysis.title: Scales Y so spectra recorded with different power, time or focus can be compared.

path: Subtract or divide by another spectrum…
menubar:analysis.label: Subtract or divide by another spectrum…
menubar:analysis.title: Combines this spectrum with another one in the project, interpolated onto this X: a dark spectrum to subtract, a lamp or white reference to divide by.

menubar:analysis.label: Average with other spectra…
menubar:analysis.title: Combines this spectrum with others in the project, each interpolated onto this one's X: repeated scans averaged into one with less noise. Points outside any spectrum's range are dropped. With the mean, the spread between the spectra can become the error bars.

menubar:analysis.label: Derivative…
menubar:analysis.title: Savitzky–Golay derivative. The second derivative turns shoulders into clear minima; both amplify noise, so the window matters.

menubar:analysis.label: Derivative, as a new column…
menubar:analysis.title: Keeps this column and adds its derivative beside it

menubar:analysis.label: Cumulative integral…
menubar:analysis.title: The running area under the curve, by trapezoids, from the low-X end: the last value is the total area. For a titration, a dose, or the fraction of a band's area below each X.

menubar:analysis.label: Smooth…
menubar:analysis.title: Reduces noise. Every smoothing lowers and broadens the narrowest bands a little; this step measures how much and warns when it matters.

menubar:analysis.label: FFT filter…
menubar:analysis.title: Filters in Fourier space. A low-pass keeps broad features and removes fast noise; a high-pass removes slow drifts and keeps the bands. The cut-off is a period in points: features narrower than it (low-pass) or wider than it (high-pass) are what is removed. The ends are mirrored so they do not ring.

menubar:analysis.label: Integrate…
menubar:analysis.title: Areas between windows you drag on the graph, each over a local baseline, without a fit

menubar:analysis.label: Python on the active column…
menubar:analysis.title: Change the data with your own code; the code and its result become a processing step

menubar:analysis.label: A new column with Python…
menubar:analysis.title: The result becomes a column of its own, a branch in the History

menubar:statistics.title: Each column's numbers, the integral of the range in view, the noise and the signal to noise

menubar:spectroscopy.label: Overview of the spectrum…
menubar:spectroscopy.title: What the spectrum is like (spacing, noise, bands, spikes, background) and what to do first

menubar:spectroscopy.label: Remove cosmic-ray spikes…
menubar:spectroscopy.title: Finds features at most a point or two wide that stand far above the noise, and replaces each by a straight line between its neighbours. Real bands are wider than a spike, so they are left alone; the graph marks every point this step changed.

menubar:spectroscopy.label: Subtract background…
menubar:spectroscopy.title: Estimates the slowly varying background under the bands (fluorescence, stray light, a sloping baseline) and subtracts it. The graph shows the input with the background drawn under it.

path: Name the peaks from known lines…
menubar:spectroscopy.label: Name the peaks from known lines…
menubar:spectroscopy.title: Each peak found takes the name of the nearest known line within a tolerance

menubar:spectroscopy.label: Energy calibration…
menubar:spectroscopy.title: Turns channel numbers into energies, E = a·channel + b (+ c·channel²): from the calibration you have, or fitted to peaks whose energies you know.

menubar:spectroscopy.label: Wavelength to Raman shift…
menubar:spectroscopy.title: Converts an X axis in nanometres to Raman shift in cm⁻¹ for the laser wavelength you give: shift = 10⁷ (1/λ₀ − 1/λ).

menubar:spectroscopy.label: Convert X units…
menubar:spectroscopy.title: Converts between wavelength, absolute wavenumber, photon energy and frequency.

menubar:spectroscopy.label: Calibrate X on reference peaks…
menubar:spectroscopy.title: Finds each reference peak near where it should be, and shifts X (one reference) or rescales it (two or more) so the peaks land on their known positions.

menubar:spectroscopy.label: Kubelka–Munk…
menubar:spectroscopy.title: F(R) = (1 − R)² / 2R, for diffuse reflectance from powders.

menubar:spectroscopy.label: Bose–Einstein correction…
menubar:spectroscopy.title: Divides out the thermal population factor, for comparing low-frequency Raman spectra at different temperatures. Stokes (positive shift) is divided by n + 1, anti-Stokes by n, with n = 1/(exp(hcν̃/kT) − 1).

History: + insert a step.label: Crop…
History: + insert a step.title: Keeps only the X range you choose; everything outside it is left out of every later step and of the fit.

History: + insert a step.label: Remove a region…
History: + insert a step.title: Takes a stretch of X out of the data, for a laser line, a detector seam or a notch-filter edge. Unlike masking, later steps never see these points.

History: + insert a step.label: Remove cosmic-ray spikes…
History: + insert a step.title: Finds features at most a point or two wide that stand far above the noise, and replaces each by a straight line between its neighbours. Real bands are wider than a spike, so they are left alone; the graph marks every point this step changed.

History: + insert a step.label: Sort by X
History: + insert a step.title: Puts the points in increasing X. Smoothing, derivatives and resampling assume ordered points.

History: + insert a step.label: Average duplicate X
History: + insert a step.title: Where the same X appears on consecutive rows, keeps one point with the mean Y (and the standard error of that mean).

History: + insert a step.label: Resample to even spacing…
History: + insert a step.title: Interpolates onto evenly spaced X. Savitzky–Golay smoothing and derivatives assume even spacing; so does comparing spectra point by point.

History: + insert a step.label: Subtract background…
History: + insert a step.title: Estimates the slowly varying background under the bands (fluorescence, stray light, a sloping baseline) and subtracts it. The graph shows the input with the background drawn under it.

History: + insert a step.label: Smooth…
History: + insert a step.title: Reduces noise. Every smoothing lowers and broadens the narrowest bands a little; this step measures how much and warns when it matters.

History: + insert a step.label: FFT filter…
History: + insert a step.title: Filters in Fourier space. A low-pass keeps broad features and removes fast noise; a high-pass removes slow drifts and keeps the bands. The cut-off is a period in points: features narrower than it (low-pass) or wider than it (high-pass) are what is removed. The ends are mirrored so they do not ring.

History: + insert a step.label: Scale and offset Y…
History: + insert a step.title: Y′ = a·Y + b: a dark level to subtract, a gain to correct, a sign to flip.

History: + insert a step.label: Scale and offset X…
History: + insert a step.title: X′ = a·X + b. With a = −1, turns anti-Stokes shifts into Stokes shifts.

History: + insert a step.label: Normalize…
History: + insert a step.title: Scales Y so spectra recorded with different power, time or focus can be compared.

path: Subtract or divide by another spectrum…
History: + insert a step.label: Subtract or divide by another spectrum…
History: + insert a step.title: Combines this spectrum with another one in the project, interpolated onto this X: a dark spectrum to subtract, a lamp or white reference to divide by.

History: + insert a step.label: Average with other spectra…
History: + insert a step.title: Combines this spectrum with others in the project, each interpolated onto this one's X: repeated scans averaged into one with less noise. Points outside any spectrum's range are dropped. With the mean, the spread between the spectra can become the error bars.

History: + insert a step.label: Derivative…
History: + insert a step.title: Savitzky–Golay derivative. The second derivative turns shoulders into clear minima; both amplify noise, so the window matters.

History: + insert a step.label: Cumulative integral…
History: + insert a step.title: The running area under the curve, by trapezoids, from the low-X end: the last value is the total area. For a titration, a dose, or the fraction of a band's area below each X.

History: + insert a step.label: Histogram…
History: + insert a step.title: Counts how many values fall in each bin: the distribution of the Y values (or the X values). The spectrum becomes the histogram, X the bins' centres and Y their counts, drawn as columns; fit a Gaussian to it for a mean and a width.

History: + insert a step.label: Kubelka–Munk…
History: + insert a step.title: F(R) = (1 − R)² / 2R, for diffuse reflectance from powders.

History: + insert a step.label: Energy calibration…
History: + insert a step.title: Turns channel numbers into energies, E = a·channel + b (+ c·channel²): from the calibration you have, or fitted to peaks whose energies you know.

History: + insert a step.label: Wavelength to Raman shift…
History: + insert a step.title: Converts an X axis in nanometres to Raman shift in cm⁻¹ for the laser wavelength you give: shift = 10⁷ (1/λ₀ − 1/λ).

History: + insert a step.label: Convert X units…
History: + insert a step.title: Converts between wavelength, absolute wavenumber, photon energy and frequency.

History: + insert a step.label: Calibrate X on reference peaks…
History: + insert a step.title: Finds each reference peak near where it should be, and shifts X (one reference) or rescales it (two or more) so the peaks land on their known positions.

History: + insert a step.label: Bose–Einstein correction…
History: + insert a step.title: Divides out the thermal population factor, for comparing low-frequency Raman spectra at different temperatures. Stokes (positive shift) is divided by n + 1, anti-Stokes by n, with n = 1/(exp(hcν̃/kT) − 1).

History: + insert a step.label: Python…
History: + insert a step.title: Your own code, run in Python in this browser. The step keeps the code and the result it produced, so the project opens with the same data without running Python again. Other spectra the code takes from spectra are recorded, drawn as dashed lines in the History, and checked: when the data coming into the step, or a spectrum it reads, change, it says so; run it again.
